title: Edge cases
objective: List the inputs that break code (empty, one item, values that cancel out) and test them on purpose.

sources.title: Myers, Sandler and Badgett, The Art of Software Testing, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2011): test-case design and boundary-value analysis

simplifies: Three edge cases are shown. Real checklists are longer: very large inputs, duplicates, negative numbers, wrong types, and the boundaries of every range in the problem.

quiz.prompt: Which input is most likely to break a function that returns the first item of a list?

options.explanation: Long lists are fine here: there's still a first item.
Right. There is no first item to return. Empty input is the classic edge case.
Negative values are still values; the first one exists.

quiz.prompt: average([]) crashes. What's a sensible fix?

options.text: Delete the test so it stops failing
options.explanation: That hides the bug instead of fixing it.

options.text: Decide what an empty list should mean (e.g. return None or raise a clear error) and handle it first
options.explanation: Right. The real fix is a decision about the edge case, written into the code and tested.
That never crashes, but it gives the wrong average for every non-empty list.
